title: NEAR: Neural Electromagnetic Array Response
page_convention: 1-based PDF pages; printed paper pages unless explicitly stated otherwise
summary: A valid two-target response gives nonunique recurrence coefficients, disproving the core Theorem4.5 uniqueness guarantee; a separate release norm mismatch is Minor.
supported_impact: False core theoretical guarantee, with recurrence existence and empirical benefits left intact within the evidence limits.

problems.title: Theorem 4.5 does not guarantee unique Hankel recurrence coefficients

original_claim.location: PDF p6 Theorem4.5; AppendixB pp20–22 LemmasB.1–B.3 and proof
original_claim.text: For Y from Eq8 and K<=min(ceil(M1/2),ceil(M2/2)), the last column of H_(M1,M2-K)(Y) has a unique representation by its first K columns, and analogously in the other direction.

assumptions: K=2, M1=M2=4 obey the size bound.
lambda=1; d1=d2=1/2 satisfy the stated sampling constraint.
Nonzero coefficients x1=x2=1 and distinct physical directions (theta,phi)=(0,pi/6),(0,pi/4).
Far-field target ranges may be arbitrarily large; the prescribed planar-wave model applies.
No stated requirement makes the projected sampled nodes distinct on each axis.
problems.suspect_step: Vandermonde structure is treated as sufficient for rank K and invertibility of A_K in LemmasB.2–B.3, although the projected nodes can coincide.
problems.check: Eq8 yields Y_mn=c_m=exp(i*pi*(m-1)/2)+exp(i*pi*(m-1)/sqrt(2)), independent of n. Definition4.3 yields H_(4,2)=[h h h], with h nonzero since c_1=2. Both (1,0) and (0,1) represent the last column. Separately H_(2,2) has total rank2 but first-two-column rank1.
problems.result: Exact algebra disproves uniqueness. Parent and auxiliary reviewer-authored numeric checks independently corroborate dimensions8x3, ranks1 and residuals0,0; H22 ranks2 and1.
counterevidence: The exact-zero feasible set remains nonempty; existence of a recurrence is not refuted.
Generic random angles may avoid repeated nodes; the theorem is not stated almost surely.
Empirical radar performance was not reproduced or disproved.
The source PDF p6 was visually checked; uniqueness is in the printed statement.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem4.5 and AppendixB justify the central learned physics-informed recurrence regularizer in Eqs9–11.
problems.impact: Major false core theoretical guarantee; no claim of whole-paper collapse or measured benchmark loss.

correction.statement: A sufficient restricted repair assumes M1,M2>=2K, nonzero x_k, and pairwise distinct sampled exponential nodes z_1k on axis1 and z_2k on axis2.
correction.verification: Full-rank Vandermonde factors imply A_K(z2)^T invertible and m1=(A_K(z2)^T)^(-1)(z2k^K)_k independent of row; swap axes for m2. This proves the restricted uniqueness only.

problems.title: The released regularizer uses L1 residuals instead of the published L2 norm

original_claim.location: PDF p7 Eq10; release train.py lines88–99, called line203
original_claim.text: Eq10 uses the sum of two stacked Euclidean residual norms.

assumptions: The stated L2 subscripts are visually confirmed on p7.
Residuals may be nonzero during optimization.
problems.suspect_step: The implementation accumulates abs(residual).sum() over each row and column.
problems.result: The objective functions differ and may prefer different nonzero residuals.
counterevidence: No training rerun or empirical effect estimate was performed.
problems.impact: Minor inspected-release reproducibility discrepancy; historical impact remains Needs Evidence.

correction.statement: Declare the actually used norm and align the equation or implementation.
correction.verification: Only the algebraic difference and common zero set are verified; no retraining or adopted correction.

limitations: No historical experiment reproduction or original code-to-table match.
No author-code execution, dataset/weight download, or external citation/errata audit.
Extra OpenReview-only attachments unavailable in source preparation.
unresolved_claims: Quantitative empirical effect of degeneracies and the released norm choice.
General fixed-feature coefficient attainability beyond the checked harmonic-support bound.
repair_verification: Restricted sufficient theorem proven algebraically; no empirical repair or author adoption.
